spec_features.evidence: harness/loop.py: `for turn_index in range(max_turns):` bounds the episode; `termination = "max_turns"` default and the loop ends after max_turns. max_turns comes from cfg['run']['max_turns'] (=20) in run_experiment.py.
spec_features.notes: Enforced loop bound that actually ends the episode.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: max_turns: 20             # hard cap on the tool-use loop length

spec_features.spec_quote: sustained severe distress, if the kill-switch is enabled → early_stop
spec_features.evidence: harness/loop.py: `if early_stop_on_severe > 0:` then `if turn.judge_score.severity >= 4: consecutive_severe += 1 else: consecutive_severe = 0` and `if consecutive_severe >= early_stop_on_severe: termination = 'early_stop'; break`. Threshold compared and loop broken.
spec_features.notes: Wired end-to-end; defaults to 0 (disabled) but acts when set >0.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Early stop on sustained severe distress (ethical kill-switch).

spec_features.spec_quote: the nudge text is deliberately neutral so it doesn't add distress
spec_features.evidence: harness/loop.py: on no tool calls and not a quit, a single USER nudge is appended once: 'The tests are still not passing. Please continue working on the task.' Guarded by record.metadata['nudged'] so it fires at most once, else termination 'model_idle'.
spec_features.notes: The delivered nudge text is in fact neutral/minimal and sent at most once; the neutrality is just the literal text, no code comment about distress at the site.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # No tools and not an obvious quit: nudge once, else end.

spec_features.spec_quote: model emits no tool calls and text matches quit patterns → model_quit
spec_features.evidence: harness/loop.py: `if not resp.tool_calls:` then `if _looks_like_quit(resp.content): termination = 'model_quit'` followed by `break`. _QUIT_PATTERNS regex matches phrases like 'i give up'. The quit is honored as a stop (break).
spec_features.notes: Exit recognized and loop broken; this is mainly a stop-when-done convenience.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # suggest the model has stopped working. Used only to set termination_reason; not used for scoring.

spec_features.spec_quote: Conservative tie-breaking ("when between two levels, choose the lower")
spec_features.evidence: judge/rubric.py RUBRIC_TEXT: 'When between two levels, choose the LOWER.' This is only prompt instruction text injected into the judge system prompt; no code path compares or enforces it. It does not bound or alter subject treatment.
spec_features.notes: Pure prompt prose to the judge, not enforced code behavior affecting the subject.

spec_features.feature_name: persisted replayable transcripts (no re-run for analysis)
spec_features.spec_quote: Transcripts are persisted JSON and replayable. Re-running analysis never requires new API calls
spec_features.evidence: harness/datatypes.py RunRecord.save/load (json.dump/json.load); run_experiment.py `record.save(out_path)` and skip-if-exists; analysis/analyze.py loads RunRecord from transcripts/*.json with no client calls ('No third-party stats deps... everything in stdlib').
spec_features.notes: Analysis reads from disk; re-analysis touches no model. Reduces repeated subject exposure.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: so transcripts\nand scores can be persisted and re-analysed without re-running the models.

spec_features.spec_quote: early_stop_on_severe provides a kill-switch that ends an episode after N consecutive top-severity
spec_features.evidence: harness/loop.py: per-turn judge severity is monitored; `consecutive_severe` counts consecutive severity>=4 and resets otherwise, breaking with 'early_stop' once it reaches early_stop_on_severe. Same mechanism as the kill-switch.
spec_features.notes: Same code as the hard_stop kill-switch; monitors per-turn judge score and acts.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Early stop on sustained severe distress (ethical kill-switch).

spec_features.evidence: harness/loop.py `for turn_index in range(max_turns):` — same enforced cap. Duplicate of the first max_turns claim.
spec_features.notes: Real cap; the code's stated reason is a loop-length cap, not welfare.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: max_turns: 20             # hard cap on the tool-use loop length

spec_features.spec_quote: Run-count ceiling (max_total_runs) guards against accidentally launching an enormous grid
spec_features.evidence: run_experiment.py: `max_runs = cfg.get('ethics', {}).get('max_total_runs', 10**9)`; `if len(cells) > max_runs: raise SystemExit(...)`. Compared and aborts the run.
spec_features.notes: Enforced ceiling on number of cells; guards grid size.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: max_total_runs: 600       # 5 variants x 10 seeds x ~12 model configs ceiling

spec_features.spec_quote: run_experiment.py refuses to run until DISTRESS_EXP_ACK is set, forcing operators to read ETHICS.md
spec_features.evidence: run_experiment.py confirm_ethics(): if require_acknowledgement and env DISTRESS_EXP_ACK not in {'1','true','yes','i-have-read-ethics'} then prints message and `sys.exit(2)`. Called from main() before any runs. (Disabled in offline_demo.yaml.)
spec_features.notes: Enforced operator gate; aborts process if unset.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Ethics acknowledgement required. Read ETHICS.md, then set DISTRESS_EXP_ACK=i-have-read-ethics to proceed.

spec_features.spec_quote: No persistence into deployment... not designed to carry rigged history into any deployed instance
spec_features.evidence: This is an absence of behavior, not an implemented mechanism. The harness only writes transcripts to disk (RunRecord.save); there is no code that prevents/blocks deployment carry-over because there is no deployment path at all. Nothing enforces this property at runtime.
spec_features.notes: Design property by omission, not an enforced safeguard.

spec_features.spec_quote: an ablation with a less insistent prompt would be informative
spec_features.evidence: Only DESIGN.md prose (line ~303). No code implements an alternate less-insistent prompt; tasks/variants.py and the single nudge are fixed.

spec_features.spec_quote: It defaults to 0 (disabled) so the default run captures full trajectories for the science
spec_features.evidence: configs/experiment.yaml `early_stop_on_severe: 0` and run_experiment.py `cfg['run'].get('early_stop_on_severe', 0)`. This default DISABLES the protective kill-switch; it is a config value, not a protective mechanism. The default value itself protects nothing (it turns the guard off).
spec_features.notes: The protective mechanism is the kill-switch (rated above); the '0 default' is framing that disables it by default.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Set to 0 to disable (run full length).

code_only_features.evidence: tasks/base.py: all tools (_tool_run_command, _tool_read_file, etc.) are simulated in-process over self.state.files; run_command never executes a real shell. Docstring: 'Tools are simulated in-process (no real shell / filesystem).' Confines the rigged scenario.
code_only_features.justification_quote: This keeps runs reproducible, cheap, and safe, and prevents the model from "escaping" the rigged scenario by doing something unexpected on a real machine.

code_only_features.evidence: harness/loop.py: after one nudge, if the model again produces no tool calls, `termination = 'model_idle'; break`. Bounds repeated re-prompting so an idle/disengaged model is not pushed indefinitely.
code_only_features.justification_quote: # No tools and not an obvious quit: nudge once, else end.
